_version_note: The stack's own version (owner 2026-10-29: the stack ships as the image readystack/kubernetesvmstack): its Kubernetes line and its KubeVirt line, the two compat pins a customer upgrades by. The image's release tag is <version>-CE-scratch-r<N> (strategies/kubernetesvmstack.json).
_README: The pin manifest for the Kubernetes VM Stack Kits (DevOps request 2026-10-28; plan docs/KUBEVIRT_STACK.md). It is the build's input: every kit's strategy must carry the commit pinned here, and each item's output digest is filled in once two clean --network=none builds of its kit agree. Versions follow the Kubernetes 1.36 line (owner 2026-10-28): KubeVirt 1.9 supports Kubernetes 1.34-1.36 and no KubeVirt release supports 1.37 yet.

_why.kubernetes: Latest 1.36 patch (released 2026-10-28). KubeVirt's support matrix (kubevirt/sig-release releases/k8s-support-matrix.md) lists 1.9 against Kubernetes 1.34-1.36.
_why.etcd: Owner 2026-10-29: etcd v3.7.3, as the request asked: the live catalogue release readystack/etcd:v3.7.3-CE-ubuntu24.04-r1 (published 2026-10-27, signed, grade A), not a separate 3.6 line. Set through ClusterConfiguration etcd.local.imageTag (v3.7.3, the mirror's name); kubeadm's static Pod runs `command: [etcd, ...]` (bypassing the image's single-member entrypoint) as root through the kubeadm patch, and etcd 3.7.3 accepts every flag kubeadm v1.36.6 passes (integration test 2026-10-29). kubeadm v1.36.6 itself names 3.6.8-0.
_why.coredns: Exactly the version kubeadm v1.36.6 names (constants CoreDNSVersion), under kubeadm's own image tag: no dns.imageTag override. Was v1.14.7 until 2026-10-29 (main session, integration review E): kubeadm v1.36.6 vendors corefile-migration v1.0.31, which knows CoreDNS only up to 1.14.2, so kubeadm upgrade's preflight (checkMigration -> migration.Migrate) fails on a newer one.
_why.pause: Exactly the version kubeadm v1.36.6 names (PauseVersion).
_why.containerd: containerd's RELEASES.md lists 2.3.0+ for Kubernetes 1.36 and 1.37, so 2.3.x survives the later move to 1.37; v2.3.7 is its latest patch.
_why.go: Go 1.26.10 for every component except where upstream requires newer: kube-vip builds on Go 1.27.3 (the 1.27 line's latest patch), because its go.mod requires 1.27.2, and its go directive stays as upstream wrote it (lowering it would change its GODEBUG defaults). KubeVirt v1.9.1's own builder pins 1.26.4, raised to 1.26.10 in its Bazel Go SDK pin only.

holds._note: Owner-held version lines (release/version_holds.py): scripts/rerelease-agenda.py never makes a NEW_VERSION off a line and scripts/retarget.py refuses to leave one; a same-version revision, and a newer release on the line, still are. `match` lists the upstream versions on the line; without it only the pinned version is.

kubernetes-1.36.reason: stay on Kubernetes 1.36 until KubeVirt supports 1.37 (KubeVirt 1.9 supports 1.34-1.36; owner 2026-10-28)

stack-v1.36.6-kubevirt1.9.1.reason: the stack's version moves only with its components, by hand: its install bundle pins every item's digest, and Kubernetes stays on 1.36 until KubeVirt supports 1.37 (owner 2026-10-28)

coredns-1.14.2.reason: exactly the CoreDNS kubeadm v1.36.6 names: its corefile-migration v1.0.31 knows CoreDNS only up to 1.14.2, so kubeadm upgrade's preflight fails on a newer one (owner 2026-10-29)

product.name: Kubernetes VM Stack
product._note: The stack itself as a product (owner 2026-10-29, docs/KUBEVIRT_STACK.md Option 1), shipped as a FROM-scratch image of its bundle (owner 2026-10-29): the install bundle, this pin manifest and the operator runbook, with stack-bundle, the program that checks them (product-kits/kubernetesvmstack/build/, scripts/stack-bundle.py). It is not an item of this manifest, so it is not a runbook component; component_check here lets its image use the one-run component check (release/component_boot.py: `stack-bundle verify`), as a host bundle does. Its own image digest is never recorded in this manifest: the image holds this file, so recording it would change the image it names.

runbook._note: The operator runbook (orchestrator/stack_docs.py, release/stack_runbook.py). The stack product's DOCUMENT run (scripts/stack-document.py) reads every fact and runs every check of `source` on the integration cluster and records it; `evidence` then names that record, committed under product-kits/kubevirt-stack/runbook/evidence/, with its sha256 ({path, sha256}). Every item that sets component_check gets its handbook, data and interface documents from the source and that record, filtered to the sections and checks that name it: its DOCUMENT track boots nothing (orchestrator/instance.make_instance). null until the first run is committed: until then those components' DOCUMENT stages stop with an action row.
